ground_truth_facts: Redis is predominantly single-threaded for command execution using an I/O multiplexing event loop.
Cache-Aside pattern requires reading from cache first, falling back to database, and writing to cache.
Eviction policies include LRU (Least Recently Used), LFU (Least Frequently Used), and TTL-based expiration.
Thundering herd problem occurs when multiple clients query DB simultaneously upon cache miss/expiration.
Kafka organizes events into topics partitioned across cluster brokers for horizontal scalability.
Consumer groups enable parallel processing while guaranteeing ordered event consumption per partition.
Replication factor ensures fault tolerance by replicating topic partitions across leader and follower nodes.
At-least-once delivery guarantees require idempotent consumer processing to prevent duplicate operations.
Sharding distributes database rows across distinct database instances using a shard key.
Consistent Hashing minimizes key remapping during cluster node scale-out or scale-in events.
Cross-shard JOIN operations are computationally expensive and generally avoided in high-throughput architectures.
Distributed transactions across shards require 2-Phase Commit (2PC) or Saga pattern to maintain consistency.
CAP theorem states a distributed system can simultaneously provide at most two of Consistency, Availability, and Partition Tolerance.
PACELC theorem extends CAP by stating: If Partition, choose Availability or Consistency; Else, choose Latency or Consistency.
Strong Consistency (Linearizability) guarantees all reads return the latest written value.
Eventual Consistency guarantees all replicas converge to identical state given no new updates.

topic: Rate Limiting Algorithms & API Gateway Architecture
ground_truth_facts: Token Bucket algorithm allows bursty traffic up to bucket capacity while refilling tokens at fixed rate.
Leaky Bucket algorithm processes requests at a constant output rate regardless of incoming traffic spikes.
Sliding Window Log algorithm provides high precision rate limiting but incurs higher memory overhead.
API Gateways use Redis or memcached as centralized atomic counters for distributed rate limiting.
